RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Rowan Delgado
Member ID: W865123628
Reference Number: POC-9391F374E1-41425
Date of Notice: 2026-08-18
Requested Service/CPT: Cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551

To the BCBSND Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 22551 (anterior cervical discectomy and fusion), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." The notice did not identify the specific medical policy or clinical criteria applied to reach that conclusion. Based on my own review of BCBSND's publicly posted provider medical policy library, the policy that appears to govern this CPT code is:

- Title: "Cervical Fusions"
- Policy ID: "S-9004-02"
- Section: "Surgery"
- Effective Date: "July 06, 2020"; Revised Date: "May 20, 2024"; Revision Effective Date: "July 01, 2024"; Last Reviewed: "May 14, 2024"
- Applies To: "Commercial and Medicaid Expansion"

I am not able to confirm that this is the exact policy version BCBSND's reviewer relied on, since the denial notice itself did not cite a policy number or quote the criteria applied. I respectfully request that BCBSND identify, in its response to this appeal, the specific policy title, number, and version used, and provide me a copy of the exact criteria applied, if different from what is quoted below.

Applying the criteria set out in the "Cervical Fusions" policy for anterior cervical fusion for degenerative disease, which states that ACDF "is considered medically necessary for treatment of symptomatic degenerative disease when ALL of the following criteria are met: unremitting cervical radiculopathy and/or myelopathy (i.e., neck and arm pain) resulting in disability and/or neurological deficit that are refractory to at least six weeks of standard conservative, nonoperative management (e.g., reduced activities, exercise, analgesics, physical therapy), in the absence of progressive or severe myelopathy[;] complex imaging studies (i.e., CT, MRI, X-ray) demonstrate at least ONE of the following at each impacted level being considered for the fusion: Herniated nucleus pulposus[;] Spondylosis (i.e., presence of osteophytes)[;] Visible loss of disc height compared to adjacent levels with resultant foraminal stenosis[;] physical examination findings and imaging studies correlate with each level being considered for the fusion" — my clinical record demonstrates that each of these elements is met:

1. Unremitting radiculopathy refractory to at least six weeks of conservative management:
   My symptoms have been present for 14 months of progressive neck pain, unrelieved by rest, with radicular pain and numbness radiating into the right thumb and index finger, accompanied by weakness. I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits, 2026-05-18 through 2026-07-13), including cervical traction and postural training, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note — well in excess of the six-week minimum referenced in the policy. I have also used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08 that produced only 3 weeks of partial relief. This treatment course establishes that my symptoms have been refractory to standard nonoperative management.

2. Imaging demonstrating a qualifying finding at the level considered for fusion:
   MRI of the cervical spine dated 2026-06-26 documents a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. This satisfies the imaging criterion, which requires demonstration of "Herniated nucleus pulposus" (among other qualifying findings) at the level being considered for fusion.

3. Correlation between physical examination findings and imaging studies:
   On examination, I have positive provocative testing on the affected (right) side and a neurologic deficit — sensory changes in the right thumb and index finger with associated weakness — that corresponds to the C6 distribution shown on imaging to be compressed at C5-C6. This is a direct clinical-radiographic correlation at the level proposed for surgery, as required by the policy.

In addition, I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, and I am a non-smoker, which removes any concern related to the tobacco-use considerations addressed elsewhere in BCBSND's spinal fusion policies.

Because the record satisfies each element of the policy's medical-necessity criteria for single-level ACDF for degenerative disease, I respectfully request that BCBSND reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 22551, as recommended by my treating surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD (orthopedic surgery).

Enclosed with this appeal are the following supporting records:
- Physical therapy discharge note (8 weeks, 18 visits, 2026-05-18 to 2026-07-13)
- Medication and injection history (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-08)
- MRI cervical spine report dated 2026-06-26
- Clinical examination notes documenting provocative testing and neurologic deficit
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Marchetti, MD
- [Any additional records the surgeon's office chooses to include]

Please treat this as a formal internal appeal under my plan. I understand from the denial notice that this appeal must be received by 2027-02-14. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the expected timeframe for a decision. If any additional information is needed, please contact me at [phone number] or [email address], or my authorized representative, Dr. Marchetti's office, at [office phone number].

If this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, I intend to pursue all further appeal rights available to me, including an external review, and I request that BCBSND include instructions for requesting external review with its response.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Rowan Delgado
Member ID: W865123628
